## What The Business Is

Strategy Inc. (formerly MicroStrategy) is now primarily a **Bitcoin treasury company** with a legacy enterprise analytics/software business. Management describes the core model as raising capital through common equity, preferred equity/“digital credit,” and other instruments to accumulate and hold bitcoin over the long term. In its Q1 2026 materials, Strategy said it held **818,334 BTC** as of early May 2026, representing about **3.9% of the maximum bitcoin supply**, and characterized itself as the largest corporate bitcoin holder. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1050446/000105044626000024/mstr-20260505x8kxex991.htm?utm_source=openai))

## What It Does

Operationally, Strategy still sells analytics and application software, but the market’s focus is overwhelmingly on its bitcoin balance sheet and capital-markets engine. The Q1 2026 call excerpt emphasizes management’s objective to grow **bitcoin per share** via repeated BTC purchases funded by securities issuance, while keeping leverage “modest” relative to the bitcoin reserve. The company has also built a stack of preferred securities—STRF, STRC, STRK, STRD—positioned by management as “Digital Credit” products backed by Strategy’s bitcoin-heavy capital structure. ([assets.contentstack.io](https://assets.contentstack.io/v3/assets/bltf8d808d9b8cebd37/bltb120ca8ac738e134/69fa4a3250829712e58cb255/strategy-q1-2026-financial-results.pdf?utm_source=openai))

## Recent Highlights (Positive)

Strategy continued adding bitcoin after Q1. On June 8, 2026, it disclosed **845,256 BTC** held after buying **1,550 BTC** during June 1–7, funded by ATM proceeds, with aggregate BTC cost of about **$64.0B** and average cost around **$75,680/BTC**. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1050446/000119312526260709/mstr-20260504.htm?utm_source=openai))

The company kept expanding its capital toolkit. On June 29, 2026, Strategy announced a **Digital Credit Capital Framework**, a USD reserve policy, a higher STRC dividend policy, up to **$1.0B** of repurchase authorization for digital-credit securities, up to **$1.0B** for MSTR common repurchases, and a BTC monetization program. Management framed the framework as designed to strengthen preferred securities, enhance liquidity, and preserve long-term bitcoin exposure. ([markets.financialcontent.com](https://markets.financialcontent.com/stocks/article/bizwire-2026-6-29-strategy-announces-digital-credit-capital-framework-usd-reserve-policy-strc-dividend-policy-digital-credit-and-mstr-repurchase-authorizations-and-btc-monetization-program?utm_source=openai))

Strategy also rebuilt liquidity late in June: disclosures around June 22 reported **847,363 BTC** and a **$1.4B USD Reserve**, and coverage noted the reserve later increased to roughly **$2.55B** as part of the new framework. ([strategy.com](https://www.strategy.com/press/strategy-increases-its-usd-reserve-to-1-4-billion-and-btc-reserve-to-847363_06-22-2026?utm_source=openai))

## Recent Highlights (Negative)

Q1 2026 results showed the downside of fair-value bitcoin accounting: Strategy reported a large operating and net loss in the transcript excerpt, driven mainly by a decline in bitcoin’s quarter-end fair value. The company’s Q1 release said digital assets had a market value of about **$64.1B** as of May 1, but quarter-end results reflected earlier bitcoin weakness. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1050446/000105044626000024/mstr-20260505x8kxex991.htm?utm_source=openai))

The capital structure is increasingly complex and cash-demanding. Preferred securities carry high dividend obligations; recent disclosures raised STRC’s annualized dividend rate to **12.00%** for semi-monthly periods beginning July 2026, and management now explicitly evaluates BTC monetization as one tool to support obligations and capital allocation. ([markets.financialcontent.com](https://markets.financialcontent.com/stocks/article/bizwire-2026-6-29-strategy-announces-digital-credit-capital-framework-usd-reserve-policy-strc-dividend-policy-digital-credit-and-mstr-repurchase-authorizations-and-btc-monetization-program?utm_source=openai))

A notable shift occurred in early July: Strategy disclosed bitcoin sales to fund preferred dividends, with reports citing **3,588 BTC sold for about $216M**. That contrasts with the company’s historical “buy and hold” narrative and may increase scrutiny of whether future preferred obligations require more BTC monetization during weak market conditions. ([bitcoinmagazine.com](https://bitcoinmagazine.com/news/strategy-mstr-sells-3588-bitcoin?utm_source=openai))

The common stock was also volatile: one recent market report said MSTR fell **45.4% in June 2026**, reflecting sensitivity to bitcoin prices, preferred-dividend concerns, and changing perceptions of the treasury model. ([fool.com](https://www.fool.com/investing/2026/07/05/why-strategy-inc-plunged-in-june/?utm_source=openai))

## Bull Case
- Bitcoin treasury scale (~847k BTC, ~3.9% of max supply) gives MSTR unmatched leverage to any BTC recovery; a rebound in bitcoin would re-rate equity far above NAV-implied levels, as it has historically.
- The new Digital Credit Capital Framework, $2.55B USD reserve, and $1B common + $1B preferred repurchase authorizations add liquidity buffers and shareholder-return optionality that didn't exist before.
- Legacy software business (~$490M revenue) is roughly FCF-breakeven, so operating cash burn is minimal; the equity story doesn't depend on operating cash flow.
- BTC-per-share accretion via ATM issuance continues to compound the core treasury metric.

## Bear Case
- The stock fell ~45% in June 2026 and the company broke its "never sell" narrative by selling 3,588 BTC (~$216M) to fund preferred dividends — a signal that the capital structure is cash-strained.
- STRC dividend raised to 12% annualized; the preferred stack creates large, recurring cash obligations that force BTC monetization precisely in weak markets (reflexive downside).
- Fair-value BTC accounting produced a −$12.2B TTM net loss; further BTC weakness compounds losses and pressures the premium-to-NAV that funds the flywheel.
- Operating FCF remains negative (−$88M TTM) and revenue is stagnant, so the software business provides no cushion.

## Logic
- **Forward FCF:** TTM FCF is −$88.3M (vs. −$104.7M a year ago). Revenue is flattish and cost discipline is improving slightly; I project 12-month forward operating FCF of **−$70M**.
- **Applied multiple:** With structurally negative FCF, the market prices MSTR on its BTC balance sheet, not FCF, so the EV/FCF multiple is a residual. Current EV/FCF is ~−455x; the 1-year average FCF/EV of −0.17% implies roughly −500x to −590x. Given June's 45% drawdown, dividend strain, and forced BTC sales, I assume EV compresses modestly from $40.2B to ~$35.0B — an implied applied multiple of **−500x** on −$70M forward FCF (−500 × −70 = $35,000M EV).

- Sanity check: this sits within the 3-year market-cap band (mean $47.9B, std $33.4B) and reflects a ~15% discount to today's $34.1B cap, consistent with dividend-driven overhang absent a BTC rally.

## Bull Case
- Strategy holds ~847k BTC (~3.9% of max supply); any bitcoin recovery flows almost dollar-for-dollar into EV. At even a partial retrace of the June selloff, EV could re-rate 30–50% higher.
- The new Digital Credit Capital Framework ($2.55B USD reserve, $1B common buyback, $1B preferred buyback) reduces forced-seller risk and could narrow the discount to BTC NAV.
- Legacy software business still generates ~$490M revenue and near-breakeven cash flow, providing a small operating cushion; ATM access remains open for accretive BTC-per-share issuance if the premium returns.

## Bear Case
- The buy-and-hold narrative is broken: 3,588 BTC sold (~$216M) in July to fund preferred dividends. STRC's dividend was raised to 12%, escalating fixed cash obligations against a volatile asset base.
- Stock fell 45% in June; if BTC weakness persists, a reflexive doom loop is possible — falling NAV → more BTC sales for dividends → further loss of premium → impaired capital-raising ability.
- Fair-value BTC accounting produced a -$12.2B TTM net loss; FCF has been negative three straight years and preferred obligations are growing, so operating cash flow is structurally strained.

## Logic
1. **Forward FCF:** TTM FCF is -$88.3M. The software business is roughly stable, and the USD reserve/framework should modestly dampen cash burn, but higher preferred dividend servicing offsets improvement. I estimate forward FCF of **-$75M**.
2. **Applied multiple:** A conventional EV/FCF multiple is not economically meaningful for a negative-FCF bitcoin treasury vehicle, so I anchor to the packet's own FCF/EV yield. The 1-year average FCF/EV yield is ~-0.0018, implying an EV/FCF "multiple" of **≈ -555×**. Applying this to forward FCF: EV = -75 × -555 ≈ **$41,625M**. This is consistent with EV holding roughly flat-to-slightly-up versus current EV of $40,168M and staying near ~0.9× estimated BTC NAV (~847k BTC at depressed prices ≈ $44B) — a reasonable base case balancing recovery optionality against monetization risk.
3. **EV-to-market-cap bridge:** Current EV minus market cap gap = 40,167.7 − 34,119.6 = **$6,048.1M** (net debt + preferreds). Forward market cap = 41,625 − 6,048 ≈ **$35,577M**.

## Bull Case
- BTC recovery: with ~847k BTC (~3.9% of max supply), even a modest 10–20% bitcoin rebound over 12 months mechanically lifts NAV by $4–8B and the equity by more, given the leveraged capital structure.
- Capital toolkit: the Digital Credit Capital Framework, $2.55B USD reserve, and $1B common buyback authorization give management levers to defend the stock and close any NAV discount.
- Software stub stabilizes: revenue is holding near ~$490M TTM and FCF burn narrowed YoY (-$104.7M → -$88.3M), suggesting a path toward breakeven-to-positive operating FCF.

## Bear Case
- Preferred dividend drag: STRC's 12% annualized rate and the broader preferred stack create heavy fixed cash obligations; the July disclosure of 3,588 BTC sold (~$216M) to fund dividends breaks the "never sell" narrative.
- Reflexivity in reverse: a 45% June drawdown shows the equity trades as levered BTC beta; further bitcoin weakness could force more BTC monetization at depressed prices, compounding NAV erosion.
- Fair-value accounting produced a -$12.2B TTM net loss; the equity can trade at or below BTC NAV (mNAV ≤ 1.0) when the capital-raising flywheel stalls.

## Logic
1. **Forward FCF:** Software revenue ~$490–500M; assume continued burn reduction from -$88M TTM to roughly **-$50M** over the next 12 months (cost discipline, no fair-value effects in FCF).
2. **Applied multiple:** Since reported FCF is negative, EV/FCF is not directly meaningful. I value the software stub on a **normalized ~$50M FCF at 20x = ~$1.0B EV** (mature analytics business, low growth), and value the balance of EV on BTC NAV.

## Bull Case
Strategy's operating software business is small but stable (~$490M revenue), and the real value driver is its ~847K BTC treasury. If bitcoin appreciates over the next 12 months, the equity market cap could re-rate sharply higher via the leveraged premium-to-NAV dynamic the stock historically enjoys. The new Digital Credit framework, USD reserve buildup (~$2.55B), and buyback authorizations ($1B common + $1B preferred) support liquidity and could tighten discount-to-NAV. Improving software FCF trend (from -$104.7M to -$88.3M TTM) plus disciplined capital markets execution could push FCF toward breakeven, and a favorable BTC tape could lift market cap well above the 3-year mean (~$47.9B).

## Bear Case
The core operating FCF remains negative (-$88.3M TTM) with no clear path to positive standalone cash generation. Preferred dividend obligations are heavy and rising (STRC now 12.00% annualized), forcing BTC sales (3,588 BTC / ~$216M in early July) that break the buy-and-hold thesis and pressure NAV. Fair-value BTC accounting produced a massive -$12.2B net loss, and MSTR fell 45.4% in June 2026 on bitcoin sensitivity and dividend concerns. If BTC weakens, forced monetization accelerates and the premium collapses, pushing market cap below the current ~$34.1B toward the low end of the historical band.

## Logic
